blindness: No model/form manifest, key, ratings, history, or other local study input inspected.
scope: All 24 responses read, all six case families covered. Repeated assertions grouped. This is bounded coverage, not exhaustive proof that every assertion is true. Pure proposed methods and primary recommendation quality are not rated.

post.evidence: Matt Post, A Call for Clarity in Reporting BLEU Scores, 2018.

chrf.evidence: Maja Popović, chrF: character n-gram F-score for automatic MT evaluation, 2015.

comet.evidence: COMET is a neural MT-evaluation framework. A reference-based configuration uses source, hypothesis and reference; checkpoint choice matters.

mbpp.evidence: Austin et al., Program Synthesis with Large Language Models, submitted August 2021, introduces MBPP for short Python programs from natural-language descriptions.

evalplus.evidence: Liu et al. 2023 introduces EvalPlus and HumanEval+ expanded tests, documenting detection of incorrect code missed by original tests.

evalrepo.evidence: The project supports both HumanEval+ and MBPP+; MBPP+ exists in later project versions. The 2023 paper abstract focuses on HumanEval+.

math.locator: Abstract and dataset description; arXiv metadata
math.evidence: Hendrycks et al. 2021 introduces MATH competition problems with worked solutions, train/test partition, subject and difficulty labels, and final-answer accuracy. The source describes high-school competitions.

imagenetc.evidence: Hendrycks and Dietterich, ICLR 2019: ImageNet-C has 15 standard corruption types on ImageNet validation images, four groups, five severities; mCE averages corruption errors normalized against AlexNet. Additional validation corruptions exist outside the standard 15.

swe.evidence: Jimenez et al. SWE-bench consists of real GitHub issues and corresponding pull requests from Python repositories. Initial arXiv submission is October 2023; ICLR conference publication is 2024.

verified.evidence: SWE-bench Verified is a human-filtered subset created with OpenAI; annotators reviewed clarity, test-patch correctness and task solvability. It evaluates coding-agent issue resolution, not human maintainer time.

alce.evidence: Gao et al. 2023, Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations, introduces ALCE and citation-quality evaluation for end-to-end retrieval and answer generation.

factscore.evidence: Min et al. 2023 introduces atomic-fact decomposition and the percentage supported by a reliable source; evaluation includes generated biographies, not physics reviews.

scifact.evidence: Wadden et al. 2020 introduces scientific claim–abstract evidence verification. The dataset has 1,409 claims and biomedical focus, with journal sources ranging from basic science to clinical medicine.

robustness_repo.evidence: Official project links CIFAR-10-C and CIFAR-100-C and states that ImageNet-C covers all 1,000 ImageNet classes.
